findings.failure_path: The bounded-sequence cap previously terminated at a human-authenticated `continuation_authorization`. It now terminates at a checkpoint the agent writes itself (`continuation_basis=existing-task-scope` plus method/evidence prose in the caller-owned task artifact). Nothing outside the agent produces the trigger and nothing verifies it: validate_extraction_review_state.py has no `continuation_basis` handling, and the new assertions in test_ai_coding_implementation_gates.sh only grep the reference text. Literal path skipping the gate: exhaust rounds 1-3 -> write the checkpoint fields -> open a fresh sequence at index 1 with a fresh candidate binding -> repeat indefinitely, with 'never erase earlier spending' also unenforced because the ledger is caller-owned. The gated party self-adjudicates the exact state that previously required authenticated human authority.
findings.smallest_fix: Keep an authenticated human state for any sequence beyond the first: allow `continuation_basis=existing-task-scope` only when the closeout ledger records cumulative rounds and the validator rejects a second sequence lacking an external authorization record.

findings.failure_path: `source_refuted_findings` lets a candidate whose final external receipt returned findings reach `ready_for_human_decision`. Every disposition, its evidence array, and the class witness are authored by the implementer being reviewed; validate_completion_dispositions checks only digest binding, ordering, coverage and string bounds (its own comment states neither record authenticates semantic truth). So real open findings are closed by writing one non-empty evidence string per occurrence, and the closeout reports the same terminal state as a clean external pass. The new fixtures only exercise well-formed refutations, so no test fails when a refutation is false.
findings.smallest_fix: Emit a distinct terminal state (e.g. `locally_refuted_pending_human`) for `completion_basis=source_refuted_findings` instead of reusing `ready_for_human_decision`, so a self-adjudicated close is not indistinguishable from an external pass.

findings.failure_path: The new guard returns `{code:5,status:"partial"}` whenever `exactState(p.codexHome, null, false)` is false during an interrupted uninstall with trash+snapshot. `exactState` is false both when public plugin state is still present and when it is unreadable, but the message says 'uninstall resume requires absent public state' and carries no `details.hostFailure` and no remediation. If the marketplace/plugin registration genuinely still exists (interruption before removal, or the user re-added it), no code path removes it during resume, so every subsequent `uninstall --yes` returns 5 forever while the user's files stay quarantined in `.trash-*`. README's new paragraph documents exit 3/4/5 for host-state-unknown, probe failure and `partial-journal` only, so the operator has no documented recovery for `partial`.
findings.smallest_fix: Distinguish unreadable state from present state (return the hostFailure form when the probe is unusable) and give the present-state case an actionable message plus a README entry describing how to clear it.

findings.failure_path: The prior rule was absolute ('A code change does not authorize a version bump'). The replacement grants version-bump and lockfile-sync authority to 'an explicitly release-scoped item in a user-approved plan'. Plans are agent-authored, so the agent can insert a release-scoped item, obtain generic plan assent, and then mutate package.json/package-lock.json with no separate confirmation — a gated mutation reached without the user ever making a release-specific decision. npm-release.md compounds this by letting the agent 'choose the next available patch version' on its own.
findings.smallest_fix: Require the release-scoped plan item to quote the user's own release request, or restore explicit confirmation before editing version fields.

findings.failure_path: The same file forbids copying real conversation text into a shared repository record, while the assent path now requires quoting the original proposal verbatim and the dual-track checkpoint requires recording 'the original authorization reference and scope' in the caller-owned task artifact — which in this repository is a committed spec/evidence file. Following both rules is impossible, and the likely resolution is that verbatim user conversation text lands in a committed artifact.
findings.smallest_fix: State explicitly that verbatim quoting is for the visible turn only and that the durable task artifact records a non-verbatim reference (id/timestamp), never conversation text.

concern_results.conclusion: Counterexamples found on all three axes. Authority: the human-authenticated `continuation_authorization` state is replaced by an agent-recorded `continuation_basis=existing-task-scope`, so the round cap is now self-waivable with no mechanical check (validate_extraction_review_state.py never inspects that field; the new shell pins only assert prose strings). Public state: the new uninstall-resume guard conflates 'present' with 'unreadable' public state and returns a terminal `partial` with no remediation text and no README coverage. Operator compatibility: README documents exit 3/4/5 for host-state-unknown/probe/partial-journal but not the new `partial` status, and the removal of the Codex version pin means capability-probe success on an old CLI now admits install paths the smoke test no longer gates.

Two containment gaps. (1) `source_refuted_findings` lets the implementer close a candidate with open external findings into `ready_for_human_decision` using self-authored evidence strings; the validator explicitly proves binding, not truth, so the gated party self-adjudicates the terminal state. (2) Release authority: docs/CONTRIBUTING.md now treats an 'explicitly release-scoped item in a user-approved plan' as authorization to bump version and lockfile, and the plan is agent-authored, so generic plan assent reaches a version mutation without confirmation. Tests would miss both: the new shell assertions are text pins, and the Python fixtures construct dispositions mechanically rather than testing false refutation.
